name: Verification Readiness Checker
description: Know whether your business will pass Meta or Google verification before you apply. This workflow scores your website and documents against the checks verifiers actually run — privacy policy, terms, matching business details — then emails and WhatsApps you a fix list so you can pass on the first try.

config.successMessage: Thanks! We are analyzing your business now.
config.formDescription: Tell us about your business so we can check your verification readiness.

notes.what: Starts your workflow when someone fills out and submits a web form you built
notes.overview: Build a public CtrlChecks form and start the workflow when someone submits structured answers, files, or intake details.
tips: Use friendly labels for submitters and stable internal names for workflow mapping.
Map answers with {{$json.customer_email}} or {{$json.data.customer_email}} after checking a test execution.
Use select or radio options for values that drive routing, approvals, reporting, or branch conditions.
Turn CAPTCHA on for public forms that can create tickets, leads, or notifications.
Require authentication only for internal or sensitive forms.
Changing an internal name after downstream nodes are mapped requires updating those mappings too.
notes.why: Collects everything the readiness check needs in one pass — details and documents together, so the client is not chased twice.

notes.what: Reads rows from an Airtable base or adds new records — like a smarter spreadsheet
notes.overview: List, get, create, update, upsert, and delete Airtable records. The resource dropdown is visual only; runtime implements record operations, not table-management APIs.
tips: Use a Personal Access Token with data.records scopes or a saved Airtable connection
Base ID plus table/tableId are required for every operation
Create/update/upsert return records/count
Upsert also returns created and updated counts
Delete returns deletedRecords/count, not top-level deleted:true
notes.why: Creates the client record up front, so the score written later attaches to a row that already exists.

notes.what: Calls any web URL and gets data back — your universal connector to the internet
notes.overview: Call an external API or webhook, optionally adding headers, query parameters, body data, and a timeout.
notes.why: Fetches the client's live site so the AI can look for the pages verifiers check. If a site blocks automated requests this returns empty and the score will be misleadingly low — check the execution log before trusting a bad score.

config.prompt: You are a compliance analyst preparing a business for Meta/Google verification. Website HTML: {{input.body}}. Business name on file: {{input.businessName}}. Uploaded documents: GST {{input.gstDocument}}, PAN {{input.panDocument}}, bank statement {{input.bankStatement}}. Check for: a visible Privacy Policy page, a visible Terms & Conditions page, a business name and address that match across the website and the documents, and a working contact page. List every issue you find as one line starting with "ISSUE:". If everything looks correct, return "NO ISSUES FOUND".

notes.what: Sends your prompt to OpenAI's ChatGPT and gets back an AI-written response
notes.overview: Calls OpenAI through the legacy LLM adapter. Prompt is the main input; Messages is only a fallback when Prompt is blank. Temperature and Memory are visible legacy fields ignored by the current executor.
notes.why: Checks the site and documents against what verifiers actually look for: privacy policy, terms, matching business details, working contact page. One 'ISSUE:' line per problem.

notes.what: Writes and runs any JavaScript you like to transform or process your data
notes.overview: Run sandboxed JavaScript once against the current workflow data and return the transformed value for downstream nodes.
tips: Always return the value the next node should receive
Default timeout is 5000ms and runtime caps at 30000ms
Use Output Schema such as {"type":"object"} only as a top-level shape hint
JavaScript has no credentials; connect downstream service node accounts separately
Do not paste API keys, tokens, or passwords into code
notes.why: Turns the issue list into a 0-100 score. Each issue costs 15 points — change that here to make the score stricter.

notes.what: Reads rows from an Airtable base or adds new records — like a smarter spreadsheet
notes.overview: List, get, create, update, upsert, and delete Airtable records. The resource dropdown is visual only; runtime implements record operations, not table-management APIs.
tips: Use a Personal Access Token with data.records scopes or a saved Airtable connection
Base ID plus table/tableId are required for every operation
Create/update/upsert return records/count
Upsert also returns created and updated counts
Delete returns deletedRecords/count, not top-level deleted:true
notes.why: Writes the score back onto the client record so it is on file for the next check.

config.prompt: Based on these readiness issues: {{input.issues}}, write 2-3 short, plain-English fixes the client should make before applying for Meta/Google verification. Keep it friendly, specific, and actionable. No jargon.

notes.what: Sends your prompt to OpenAI's ChatGPT and gets back an AI-written response
notes.overview: Calls OpenAI through the legacy LLM adapter. Prompt is the main input; Messages is only a fallback when Prompt is blank. Temperature and Memory are visible legacy fields ignored by the current executor.
notes.why: Converts the technical issues into two or three plain-English actions the client can actually carry out.

config.body:
Hi {{input.businessName}},

Your verification readiness score is {{input.score}}/100.

Here is what to fix before you apply:
{{input.fixList}}

We will keep this record on file for your next check.
config.subject: Your verification readiness score: {{input.score}}/100

notes.what: Send emails from your Gmail account or read and search messages in your inbox
notes.overview: Send, list, get, or search Gmail messages. Send recipients can be typed manually or extracted from upstream/fallback Google Sheets rows.
tips: Connect Google OAuth in Connections; do not paste tokens into workflow fields
Gmail search syntax: from:, subject:, is:unread, has:attachment
List/Search only return {id, threadId} per message â€” use a Get step with that id for full content
Body is plain text only
Get returns Gmail's raw API message; the body text is base64url-encoded inside message.payload.body.data
Use search to filter messages before getting details
notes.why: Sends the score and the fix list. This is the deliverable the client came for.

config.text: Hi {{input.businessName}}! Your verification readiness score is {{input.score}}/100. Check your email for the full fix list, or reply here with questions.

notes.what: Sends WhatsApp messages to customers via the official WhatsApp Business API
notes.overview: Send WhatsApp messages, media, locations, contact cards, approved templates, and interactive buttons/lists through the WhatsApp Business Cloud API. Connect a WhatsApp/Facebook account under Connections â€” credentials are resolved automatically. The visual panel exposes the Message resource; Contact, Conversation, Template, Campaign, and AI Agent resources are runtime-supported for advanced or AI-generated workflows.
tips: Connect a WhatsApp account under Connections â€” no access tokens entered on the node itself
Phone numbers should be in E.164 format, e.g. +12345678900
First message to a new contact must use Send Template; free-form Send Text only works inside the 24-hour customer service window
notes.why: A short WhatsApp nudge pointing at the email, for clients who will not open it otherwise.
